The vast majority of my time this session was spent researching what even I could do. generally I'm pretty experienced in cad, so I wanted to do something a little bit more advanced. After deciding to make the robot arm, I spent a lot of time thinking about how the different sections of the arm would connect and what axes motion I wanted. And how did I want it to be controlled? I sketched out all my plans in my engineering sketchbook. I'm so excited to start getting to work on CAD.

So I kinda completely redesigned the whole thing because I wanted to use cheaper motors.... I spent a lot of time researching other people's robotics arms and realized that it is possible to use cheaper smaller moters, i just have to change a few things. Now both the shoulder and the elbow motor ar on the base and I decided to get rid of the waist motor to make it even simpler and cheaper because thats one less motor and I dont need all the ball bearings.

First I spent some time fixing the design some more, I completely reworked it from the first one... than I spent hours cading, the shoulder joint was probably the hardest part to cad and ended up being a lot of trial and error. I also challenged myself this time to try and make a design that doesn't require any glue, most of the peices snap together and you need a couple screws to hold together the servos to the peices.

I finished the prototype coding! Once agian i used tinkercad because I am veruch a beginner in coding and starting with the blocks helps me a lot, i do plan to learn really code outside of tinkercade, but I didnt have enought time this week to properly start learning. The prototype code is just a bunch of potentiometers hooked up to each of the 3 motors but in the future I plan to use a stick and a potentiometer
